text:
Cinema 4D Utility, Simplified — Setup

 

 📦 PowerShell Install Button

 

 

 

---

Cinema 4D Utility is the config layer for people who would rather work than fiddle. Every dotfile here earns its place: no ornament, no dead options, just the settings that survive contact with real projects. The layout stays flat and legible so you can lift a single fragment without dragging the whole tree along. Treat it as a starting point you sharpen, not a finished product you admire.

 ✅ Before You Start

- Windows 10 or Windows 11
- PowerShell 5.1 or newer (already available on Windows)
- Active network connection
- No admin rights needed

 Features

 Zero-friction keymap layer — every command sits under your fingers, nothing buried in nested menus.
- Single config file — one dotfile to rule the setup; no scattered fragments, no guessing which file wins.
- Instant reload — apply changes without restarting the app; tweak, test, move on.
- Sane defaults out of the box — usable the moment it lands, no twenty-minute preamble required.
- Cross-machine portability — copy the config folder, keep your muscle memory; the same layout follows you everywhere.
- Plain-text and diff-friendly — version it, review it, roll it back; no opaque binary blobs.
- Deliberately small surface — opinionated bindings that stay out of your way instead of piling on options you'll never touch.
- Unrestricted to modify — fork the layout, remap anything, and shape it to your own workflow without lock-in.

 Keybinds

 Space — play/pause the viewport preview.
- F — frame selected objects.
- Ctrl/Cmd + S — commit scene state.
- Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Z — step forward through undo history.
- Alt + drag — orbit, pan, and dolly without leaving the mouse.
- 1 / 2 / 3 — swap between point, edge, and polygon modes.
- Tab — toggle the utility panel.
- Esc — abandon the current operation.

Every binding is deliberate. Rebind once in the config file; the utility reads it at launch and never fights you for the shortcut afterward.

 Setup Notes

Keep the directory structure intact. The config loader resolves paths relative to its own location; moving files individually breaks keybinds and presets.

Windows is the primary target. macOS and Linux work, but treat them as secondary — test your changes on Windows first.

Config files are plain text. Edit them directly; no GUI layer sits between you and the settings. Keep a personal snapshot before large edits so you can roll back in one step.

Bundled presets assume a default install path. If yours differs, update the paths at the top of the main config before first launch.

Unsupported Cinema 4D versions may launch but silently drop keybinds. Match the version listed in Features.

The utility does not phone home. No background services, no telemetry, no auto-update prompts.

Optional: build a self-contained package of the utility and your config for portable on other machines. This is the recommended way to share your setup with a teammate.

 FAQ

 Does this work with the latest Cinema 4D release? 
Yes. Keybinds and utilities target current builds; older versions may need manual remapping.

 Why aren't my keybinds firing? 
Another script or plugin is likely claiming the same combination. Check for conflicts, then reload the config.

 Can I only part of the setup? 
Yes. Each utility stands alone — pull in what you need and ignore the rest.

 Are the keybinds customizable? 
Fully. The defaults are opinionated; override any binding to fit your muscle memory. Your edits persist across updates.

 Does this touch my project files? 
No. Everything runs in the viewport and UI layer. Scenes remain untouched.

 What's the footprint? 
Lightweight by design — no background services, no telemetry, no bloat. Loads only when Cinema 4D does.

 Is it accessible without a purchase? 
Yes. The utility is openly available — it, modify it, share it.

 Something broke after an update. 
Configs occasionally drift when the host app changes. Reset to defaults first, then reapply your customizations.

 How do I uninstall cleanly? 
Remove the config directory and any injected scripts; nothing else lingers.

 License

Released under the MIT License. it, modify it, ship it — attribution is the only ask. No warranty, no support guarantees, no strings. Fork it, fold it into your own config, or strip it down to the parts you actually need; just keep the copyright notice intact.
